core_obligations: Identify the target category (proof lines 13471-13472): a finite projective R-module is the same thing as a summand of a finite free R-module, so the right-hand side of the statement needs no further description.
Name the functor (proof lines 13473-13474): the equivalence is given by E -> Gamma(C, E), the global sections functor.

Construct the inverse functor (proof lines 13475-13483): take the morphism of topoi f : Sh(C) -> Sh(pt) with f_* global sections and f^{-1} the constant sheaf functor, upgrade it to a morphism of ringed topoi (f, f^sharp) : (Sh(C), O) -> (Sh(pt), R) via the identity R -> f_* O, and take the inverse functor to be f^*.
The counted proof supplies both directions implicitly by exhibiting the two functors; the verification that they are mutually inverse is the author's routine closing step inside the same environment.
proof_roadmap: Recall that finite projective R-modules are exactly the summands of finite free R-modules.
Take the global sections functor E -> Gamma(C, E) as the forward equivalence.
Build the morphism of ringed topoi to the point using the identity R -> f_* O.
Its pullback f^* is the inverse functor.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies two categories: summands of finite free O-modules on a ringed site and finite projective modules over the ring of global sections (statement lines 13461-13468). The forward functor is the global sections functor, and the work is the construction of an inverse: the author forms the morphism of topoi f : Sh(C) -> Sh(pt) with f_* = Gamma(C, -) and f^{-1} the constant sheaf functor, promotes it to a morphism of ringed topoi by the identity R -> f_* O, and takes f^* as the inverse (proof lines 13475-13483). The non-formal point is this promotion to ringed topoi, which is what produces an inverse defined on R-modules. The claim is H2: one explicit construction after a standard description of finite projective modules.
